sum: Traces an agent with OpenTelemetry and scores its behaviour with prompt-defined judges, so a failure can be traced to a cause and a fix validated against the case that produced it.

evidence.se.residency: cites data_residency: self-hostable, the state leaves the machine but the operator can own the service; keys are the operator's own (byok)
evidence.se.threats: cites th and ctrl: T6/T8 introduced, controls log impl
evidence.fx.exit: artifact.format trace-log: a run log the tool writes; readable as text, structured for the tool
evidence.sf.reach: restates exec, ctrl and data_residency: the entry does not execute code itself, but self-hostable means its state reaches a service, and no egress control is recorded
evidence.ic.help: a command-line parser that prints its own usage: pyproject.toml (typer)
evidence.fx.install: only a global install is documented: README.md (pip install j)
evidence.fx.byo: the entry does not call a model provider itself, so there is no provider for the operator to substitute
evidence.fs.scope: pyproject.toml declares the installable surface for a package manager, and nothing declares an agent-facing one

pre: agreement on what counts as good behaviour
a Python application you can instrument
anti: judging whether generated code is correct, which a behavioural judge does not decide
exploratory work where the criteria are not settled
gnote: Judges are prompts, so the scorer is itself a model output and inherits the failure modes it is meant to catch. Building on OpenTelemetry means the trace is portable, which is rare enough here to be worth recording.
